# Flow Chemistry Design Brief: Hydrogenolysis of N-Diphenylmethylazetidin-3-ol to 3-Azetidinol

**Disposition: SCREEN** | Confidence: LOW

---

## (1) Proposed Flow Setup

**Reactor:** Stainless steel packed-bed reactor (PBR), 3.0 mL, 4.35 mm ID, ~202 mm length, packed with Pd(OH)₂/Al₂O₃ (Pearlman's catalyst on alumina support) as a fixed bed.

**Two inlet streams combined at a T-mixer upstream of the bed:**

| Stream | Contents | Flow Rate | Equipment |
|--------|----------|-----------|-----------|
| A (liquid) | N-Diphenylmethylazetidin-3-ol, 0.126 M in methanol | 0.1 mL/min | pump_h2_pilot |
| B (gas) | H₂ (pure) | 1.0 sccm (STP) = 0.056 mL/min in-channel at reactor conditions | mfc_h2_100 |

**Key operating parameters:**
- Temperature: 60 °C
- BPR: 21.0 bar gauge (22.0 bar absolute)
- Substrate concentration: 0.126 M (Stream A); nominal design concentration 0.1 M
- H₂ supplied: 3.54 equiv relative to substrate (calculated from STP molar flow vs. liquid molar throughput)
- Residence time: **2.727 min** (inlet/STP apparent basis: V_R / (Q_liquid + Q_gas,STP)); liquid-only space time = 30.0 min; in-channel apparent time = 19.2 min
- Superficial velocities (empty-tube, no porosity correction): liquid 0.112 mm/s, gas 0.063 mm/s

**Downstream:** Gas-liquid separator → collection vessel. A 10 µm SS frit should be installed between the reactor outlet and the BPR to capture catalyst fines.

**Deoxygenation:** Offline — sparge methanol feed with N₂ before use; purge entire flow path with N₂ (≥5 bed volumes) before H₂ introduction.

---

## (2) Why These Conditions Were Chosen

**No directly analogous flow literature was retrieved for this specific substrate.** Conditions are extrapolated from the following reaction classes:

- **N-Cbz and N-Bn hydrogenolysis in continuous flow over Pd/C or Pd(OH)₂/C packed beds** — the standard approach for debenzylation in flow uses packed-bed reactors with H₂ gas co-feed, methanol or ethanol solvent, moderate temperature (40–80 °C), and elevated back-pressure (10–30 bar) to maintain H₂ in solution. Representative examples include work by Irfan et al. on continuous-flow hydrogenation (*Chem. Eng. J.* 2011, 167, 735) and the H-Cube/ThalesNano platform literature for Pd-catalysed N-deprotections.
- **Gas-liquid-solid packed-bed hydrogenation in flow** — elevated back-pressure (here 21 bar) is used to increase dissolved H₂ concentration in methanol (estimated ~10–15 mM at 21 bar, 60 °C by Henry's law), directly addressing the gas-liquid mass transfer limitation identified in the batch protocol.
- **Temperature 60 °C** is a modest elevation above ambient to accelerate surface kinetics without risking over-reduction or solvent issues; consistent with batch protocol temperature.
- **Methanol solvent** is retained from the batch protocol; it is compatible with Pd(OH)₂ catalysis and has acceptable H₂ solubility.
- **The 21 bar BPR** is the only available pressure setpoint in the declared inventory. It is appropriate for this reaction class and suppresses gas-phase channelling by keeping more H₂ dissolved.
- **Batch limitation identified:** gas-liquid mass transfer (kLa). Flow is justified by the expected enhancement of gas-liquid interfacial area in segmented/Taylor flow through the packed bed.

> ⚠️ **No validated kinetic model exists for this substrate in flow.** The computed 51% conversion figure is a screening proxy from a first-order batch analogy (t₉₀ ≈ 96 min inferred from 38.1% conversion in 5 h batch) and should not be used as a performance guarantee.

---

## (3) Key Differences from the Batch Protocol

| Parameter | Batch | Flow |
|-----------|-------|------|
| Reactor type | Stirred vessel, H₂ atmosphere | Fixed packed bed, co-fed H₂ gas |
| Catalyst | Suspended (slurry) | Immobilised fixed bed |
| Reaction time / residence time | 5 h | 30 min liquid space time (2.7 min STP-apparent) |
| H₂ delivery | Headspace pressure, stirring-dependent kLa | Continuous co-feed at T-mixer; segmented flow in bed |
| Temperature | Ambient (assumed ~25 °C) | 60 °C |
| Pressure | Not stated (likely 1–5 bar H₂) | 21 bar gauge |
| Catalyst separation | Filtration post-reaction | Inline frit; catalyst stays in bed |
| Batch conversion | 38.1% at 5 h | Unknown — first screen |

The primary intensification hypothesis is that segmented gas-liquid flow through the packed bed increases kLa relative to the stirred batch, allowing comparable or better conversion at much shorter contact time. This is undemonstrated for this substrate and must be measured.

---

## (4) Warnings and Flags from Engineering Validation

### Safety — Mandatory Controls

1. **Flammable hydrogen at 21 bar in methanol service.** Leak-test the entire flow path with N₂ before admitting H₂. Use grounded ventilation; remove all ignition sources from the area.
2. **Shutdown sequence:** Stop H₂ MFC first → displace residual H₂ with N₂ (≥5 bed volumes) → depressurise through the controlled BPR outlet only. Never open the system under H₂ pressure.
3. **O₂ ingress is a dual hazard:** deactivates Pd(OH)₂ catalyst AND can form flammable H₂/O₂ mixtures in the separator headspace. Verify O₂ < 100 ppm at the separator vent with a calibrated electrochemical sensor before switching from N₂ to H₂.

### Engineering Flags

**DFMEA top failure modes (ranked by risk priority number):**

| RPN | Failure Mode | Mitigation |
|-----|-------------|------------|
| 48 | Gas-liquid maldistribution / dry-bed channelling at very low superficial velocities (liquid 0.11 mm/s, gas 0.063 mm/s) | Hydraulic commissioning run with solvent + N₂ before substrate; monitor pressure drop for drift |
| 45 | Catalyst fines migration blocking BPR orifice | Install 10 µm SS frit at bed outlet; weigh frit before/after; add inline pressure transducer between reactor and BPR |
| 40 | O₂ ingress causing catalyst poisoning or ignition | Documented N₂ purge protocol; O₂ sensor go/no-go gate before H₂ introduction |

**Single points of failure to note:** BPR (no bypass), MFC (sole H₂ control), single liquid pump (pump failure → dry bed under H₂ pressure with active Pd — pyrophoricity risk), gas-liquid separator (primary containment at 21 bar H₂).

### Residence Time Ambiguity

Three residence time values are reported — this is not an error, but you need to know which one applies to your chemistry:

- **2.727 min** — STP-apparent (V_R divided by liquid + gas flow at STP); used as the design reference
- **19.2 min** — in-channel apparent (gas compressed to reactor conditions)
- **30.0 min** — liquid-only space time (V_R / Q_liquid); the most physically meaningful for catalyst contact

**For kinetic interpretation, use the 30 min liquid space time.** The 2.7 min figure is a bookkeeping index, not the actual substrate contact time with the catalyst.

### Required Commissioning Experiments (Before Running Substrate)

1. **Hydraulic commissioning:** Flow methanol at 0.1 mL/min + N₂ at 1 sccm through the packed bed at 21 bar, 60 °C for 60 min. Record inlet/outlet pressure every 5 min. Flag any drift >5% as bed integrity failure.
2. **O₂ purge verification:** Confirm O₂ < 100 ppm at separator vent after N₂ purge before switching to H₂.
3. **Blank H₂ saturation run:** Run methanol + H₂ (no substrate) for 30 min at operating conditions. Measure dissolved H₂ in outlet liquid (headspace GC or mass balance) to confirm gas-liquid contacting is functional before committing substrate.

**Confidence: LOW** — The closest literature analogy has a similarity score of 0.09 (threshold for MEDIUM: 0.50). No close precedent found in the corpus for this exact reaction class and conditions. Treat this proposal as a starting hypothesis requiring careful experimental validation before scale-up.

Final engineering validation: ready.

_analogies.summary: This study describes a solid acid catalyzed liquid-phase aromatic nitration reaction using concentrated nitric acid in a continuous flow system. The reaction was conducted at 120°C in dichloroethane (DCE) solvent at 1.0 M concentration using a packed-bed reactor with a volume of 7.85 mL and a flow rate of 0.91 mL/min. The flow process achieved 90% yield compared to 92% yield in the corresponding batch reaction conducted under similar conditions (120°C, 1 hour reaction time). The continuous flow approach enabled safe handling of the highly exothermic and potentially hazardous nitration reaction with concentrated nitric acid through better heat management and containment in the packed-bed reactor format. A back-pressure regulator was required to maintain proper reaction conditions and prevent solvent vaporization at the elevated temperature.

_analogies.summary: This Chan-Lam-Evans C-N cross-coupling reaction was successfully translated from batch to continuous flow using a stainless steel flow reactor with syringe pump operation. The flow process achieved 99% yield at 90°C with a 56-minute residence time (0.48 mL/min flow rate) in 1,4-dioxane/water solvent, compared to only 70% yield in batch at 150°C for 24 hours. The flow reactor operated under 14 bar back-pressure and delivered a 25.7-fold intensification factor with a 29% improvement in yield over the batch baseline. Flow processing enabled significantly milder reaction conditions (60°C lower temperature) while dramatically improving both efficiency and product yield for this coupling transformation.

### Final Executable Design
- **Residence time:** 2.72727 min
- **Inlet/STP apparent residence time:** 2.72727 min
- **In-channel apparent residence time:** 19.2135 min
- **Total liquid flow:** 0.1 mL/min
- **Reactor volume:** 3 mL
- **Temperature:** 60 deg C
- **BPR:** 21 bar
- **Concentration:** 0.1 M
- **Residence-time basis:** inlet/STP apparent residence time
- **Assigned equipment:** Pressure-rated plunger pump, Hydrogen mass-flow controller, Hydrogen-service T-mixer, Pd(OH)2/Al2O3 micro-packed bed, Packed-bed water bath, Hydrogen-service BPR, Grounded vented liquid collection vessel, Nitrogen purge cylinder and regulator, Hydrogen non-return check valve, Dedicated hydrogen separator safe vent, Vented gas-liquid separator

validation_experiments: Hydraulic commissioning (no substrate, no H2): Flow MeOH/EtOH solvent at Q=0.1 mL/min through the packed bed with N2 at 1 sccm via the T-mixer; hold BPR at 21 bar for 60 min. Record inlet and outlet pressure every 5 min; flag any drift >5% as indicative of fines migration or channelling. Weigh the downstream frit before and after to quantify fines loss. This establishes baseline dP and confirms bed integrity before any H2 or substrate is introduced.

O2 purge verification: After N2 purge (≥5 bed volumes), sample the separator vent gas with a calibrated electrochemical O2 sensor; confirm O2 <100 ppm before switching to H2. Repeat the O2 check at the collection vessel headspace. Document purge volume and time as a commissioning record and go/no-go gate for H2 introduction.

Blank solvent H2 saturation run (no substrate): With the bed purged and N2 confirmed <100 ppm O2, introduce H2 at 1 sccm and MeOH at 0.1 mL/min for 30 min at 60°C/21 bar. Collect outlet liquid and measure dissolved H2 by headspace GC or pressure-drop mass balance to confirm H2 is dissolving into the liquid phase (not bypassing as free gas). This validates the gas-liquid contacting efficiency before committing substrate and provides a kLa proxy for the actual operating point.
